In [[mathematics]], specifically [[algebraic topology]], there is a resolution analogous to [[free resolution]]s of [[Spectrum (topology)|spectra]] yielding a tool for constructing the [[Adams spectral sequence]]. Essentially, the idea is to take a [[connective spectrum]] of finite type <math>X</math> and iteratively resolve with other spectra that are in the homotopy kernel of a map resolving the cohomology classes in <math>H^*(X;\mathbb{Z}/p)</math> using [[Eilenberg–Maclane spectrum|Eilenberg–MacLane spectra]].

This construction can be generalized using a spectrum <math>E</math>, such as the [[Brown–Peterson cohomology|Brown–Peterson spectrum]] <math>BP</math>, or the [[complex cobordism]] spectrum <math>MU</math>, and is used in the construction of the [[Adams–Novikov spectral sequence]]<ref name=":0" /><sup>pg 49</sup>.

== Construction ==
The mod <math>p</math> Adams resolution <math>(X_s,g_s)</math> for a spectrum <math>X</math> is a certain "chain-complex" of spectra induced from recursively looking at the fibers of maps into generalized [[Eilenberg–MacLane spectra|Eilenberg–Maclane spectra]] giving generators for the cohomology of resolved spectra<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Ravenel, Douglas C.|author-link=Douglas Ravenel|title=Complex cobordism and stable homotopy groups of spheres|date=1986|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-08-087440-1|location=Orlando|oclc=316566772}}</ref><sup>pg 43</sup>. By this, we start by considering the map<blockquote><math>\begin{matrix}
X \\
\downarrow \\
K
\end{matrix}</math></blockquote>where <math>K</math> is an Eilenberg–Maclane spectrum representing the generators of <math>H^*(X)</math>, so it is of the form<blockquote><math>K = \bigvee_{k=1}^\infty \bigvee_{I_k} \Sigma^kH\mathbb{Z}/p  </math></blockquote>where <math>I_k</math> indexes a basis of <math>H^k(X)</math>, and the map comes from the properties of [[Eilenberg–Maclane spectrum|Eilenberg–Maclane spectra]]. Then, we can take the [[homotopy fiber]] of this map (which acts as a homotopy kernel) to get a space <math>X_1</math>. Note, we now set <math>X_0 = X</math> and <math>K_0 = K</math>. Then, we can form a [[commutative diagram]]<blockquote><math>\begin{matrix}
X_0 & \leftarrow & X_1 \\
\downarrow & & \\
K_0
\end{matrix}</math></blockquote>where the horizontal map is the fiber map. Recursively iterating through this construction yields a commutative diagram<blockquote><math>\begin{matrix}
X_0 & \leftarrow & X_1 & \leftarrow & X_2 & \leftarrow \cdots \\
\downarrow & & \downarrow & & \downarrow \\
K_0 & & K_1 & & K_2
\end{matrix}</math></blockquote>giving the collection <math>(X_s,g_s)</math>. This means<blockquote><math>X_s = \text{Hofiber}(f_{s-1}:X_{s-1} \to K_{s-1})</math></blockquote>is the [[homotopy fiber]] of <math>f_{s-1}</math> and <math>g_s:X_s \to X_{s-1}</math> comes from the universal properties of the homotopy fiber.

=== Resolution of cohomology of a spectrum ===
Now, we can use the Adams resolution to construct a free <math>\mathcal{A}_p</math>-resolution of the cohomology <math>H^*(X)</math> of a spectrum <math>X</math>. From the Adams resolution, there are short exact sequences<blockquote><math>0 \leftarrow H^*(X_s) \leftarrow H^*(K_s) \leftarrow H^*(\Sigma X_{s+1}) \leftarrow 0</math></blockquote>which can be strung together to form a long [[exact sequence]]<blockquote><math>0 \leftarrow H^*(X) \leftarrow H^*(K_0) \leftarrow H^*(\Sigma K_1)
\leftarrow H^*(\Sigma^2 K_2) \leftarrow \cdots </math></blockquote>giving a free resolution of <math>H^*(X)</math> as an <math>\mathcal{A}_p</math>-module.

== ''E''<sub>*</sub>-Adams resolution ==
Because there are technical difficulties with studying the [[cohomology ring]] <math>E^*(E)</math> in general<ref name=":02">{{Cite book|last=Adams, J. Frank (John Frank)|title=Stable homotopy and generalised homology|date=1974|publisher=University of Chicago Press|isbn=0-226-00523-2|location=Chicago|oclc=1083550}}</ref><sup>pg 280</sup>, we restrict to the case of considering the homology coalgebra <math>E_*(E)</math> (of co-operations). Note for the case <math>E = H\mathbb{F}_p</math>, <math>H\mathbb{F}_{p*}(H\mathbb{F}_p) =\mathcal{A}_*</math> is the [[dual Steenrod algebra]]. Since <math>E_*(X)</math> is an <math>E_*(E)</math>-comodule, we can form the bigraded group<blockquote><math>\text{Ext}_{E_*(E)}(E_*(\mathbb{S}), E_*(X))</math></blockquote>which contains the <math>E_2</math>-page of the Adams–Novikov spectral sequence for <math>X</math> satisfying a list of technical conditions<ref name=":0" /><sup>pg 50</sup>. To get this page, we must construct the <math>E_*</math>-Adams resolution<ref name=":0" /><sup>pg 49</sup>, which is somewhat analogous to the cohomological resolution above. We say a diagram of the form<blockquote><math>\begin{matrix}
X_0 & \xleftarrow{g_0} & X_1 & \xleftarrow{g_1} & X_2 & \leftarrow \cdots \\
\downarrow & & \downarrow & & \downarrow \\
K_0 & & K_1 & & K_2
\end{matrix}</math></blockquote>where the vertical arrows <math>f_s: X_s \to K_s</math> is an <math>E_*</math>-Adams resolution if

# <math>X_{s+1} = \text{Hofiber}(f_s)</math> is the [[homotopy fiber]] of <math>f_s</math>
# <math>E \wedge X_s</math> is a retract of <math>E\wedge K_s</math>, hence <math>E_*(f_s)</math> is a [[monomorphism]]. By retract, we mean there is a map <math>h_s:E \wedge K_s \to E \wedge X_s</math> such that <math>h_s(E\wedge f_s) = id_{E \wedge X_s}</math>
# <math>K_s</math> is a retract of <math>E \wedge K_s</math>
# <math>\text{Ext}^{t,u}(E_*(\mathbb{S}), E_*(K_s)) = \pi_u(K_s)</math> if <math>t = 0</math>, otherwise it is <math>0</math>

Although this seems like a long laundry list of properties, they are very important in the construction of the spectral sequence. In addition, the retract properties affect the structure of construction of the <math>E_*</math>-Adams resolution since '''<u>we no longer need to take a wedge sum of spectra for every generator</u>'''.

=== Construction for ring spectra ===
The construction of the <math>E_*</math>-Adams resolution is rather simple to state in comparison to the previous resolution for any associative, commutative, connective ring spectrum <math>E</math> satisfying some additional hypotheses. These include <math>E_*(E)</math> being flat over <math>\pi_*(E)</math>, <math>\mu_*</math> on <math>\pi_0</math> being an isomorphism, and <math>H_r(E; A)</math> with <math>\mathbb{Z} \subset A \subset \mathbb{Q}</math> being finitely generated for which the unique ring map<blockquote><math>\theta:\mathbb{Z} \to \pi_0(E)</math></blockquote>extends maximally.

If we set<blockquote><math>K_s = E \wedge F_s</math></blockquote>and let<blockquote><math>f_s: X_s \to K_s</math></blockquote>be the canonical map, we can set<blockquote><math>X_{s+1} = \text{Hofiber}(f_s)</math></blockquote>Note that <math>E</math> is a retract of <math>E \wedge E</math> from its [[ring spectrum]] structure, hence <math>E \wedge X_s</math> is a retract of <math>E \wedge K_s = E \wedge E \wedge X_s</math>, and similarly, <math>K_s</math> is a retract of <math>E\wedge K_s</math>. In addition<blockquote><math>E_*(K_s) = E_*(E)\otimes_{\pi_*(E)}E_*(X_s)</math></blockquote>which gives the desired <math>\text{Ext}</math> terms from the flatness.

==== Relation to cobar complex ====
It turns out the <math>E_1</math>-term of the associated Adams–Novikov spectral sequence is then [[cobar complex]] <math>C^*(E_*(X))</math>.
